It should have Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) for examination of coronary arteries in patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography. 2. It should also perform Intra Vascular Ultrasound (IVUS) examination of corona ry arteries in patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography. 3. It should be able to detect the lipid-core-containing plaques of interest. It sho uld be able to assess the coronary artery lipid core burden. 4. It should be able to help in identification of patients and plaques at increased risk of major adverse cardiac events. 5. The imaging engine should be based on the fiber optic technology and ultras ound transducer. 6. It should have Two monitors, one at least 21.5” 1080p FHD monitor (1920 x1 030p) in size and one at least 15.6" 1080p FHD capacitive touch monitor (1920 x 1080p) for view and control. 7. It should have an integrated drive-motor Controller (IMC) 8. It should have an isolation transformer 9. It should have a user interface designed for both touch screen and mouse int

eraction 10. It should have Blu-Ray/DVD/CD Optical Media Drive, 02 USB port 3.0 11. It should have Configuration to export a color video signal of 1920x1080p (1 6:9 aspect ratio) using a shielded DVI-D video cable. Optionally, the exported vi deo resolution can be configured to 1600 x 1200 (4:3 aspect ratio). 12. The System should be capable to export images in DICOM and AVI Formats 13. The System should have the following DICOM capability 13.1 DICOM Storage in PACS 13.2 DICOM Media 13.3 DICOM Modality Worklist 14. The System Should be capable of DICOM compression for export 15. The System Should be compatible with IPv4 16. It should meet all applicable safety standards and functional requirements o f IEC 60601-1 17. The System should comply with laser safety standards (Class 1M) IEC 60825 -1 18. The System should be capable of managing user accounts, privileges, and p ermissions 19. The system should allow the user to Acquire, save and subsequently retriev e images for review of artery lumen and artery walls.

20. It should allow user to obtain automatic, histology validated, plaque charact erization assessment after automatic pullback of catheter. 21. It should show mxLCBl (Lipid Core Burden Index) automatically after pullbac k. 22. It should have capability to measure of diameters and areas of artery lumen or artery walls 23. It should have capability to measure distance or lengths between references and assess area stenosis 24. It should have capability to add text annotations. 25. It should have full range of playback control and subsegment playback cont rol 26. It Should be able to export still images and movies in native format or in sta ndard image formats. 27. It should be able to perform file management functions. 28. It should have configurable export functions to Network, USB, or custom app lications including anonymize data. 29. It should be Tolerant of power interruptions. 30. The imaging catheter parameters of the system should be. 30.1 The catheter should emit near infra-red light to produce an automatic, hist ology validated, plaque characterization assessment and a piezo-electric crystal to generate a High Definition (HD) resolution real-time cross-sectional ultrasoun d image using extended bandwidth of ultrasound frequencies of 35MHz to 65MH z frequency, inclusive.

30.2 Minimum frame rate of 30 fps 30.3 Pull back or available scan length of up to 150 mm 30.4 Working length of 160 cm 30.5 Auto pullback speeds up to 2.0 mm/sec 30.6 Manual pullback speed up to 10 mm/sec 30.7 Scan Image diameter: 16 mm 30.8 IVUS Image Axial resolution: 20 microns 30.9 Compatible with 0.014" (maximum OD) intervention guide wires 30.10 Compatible with a 6F (minimum 0,067" ID) interventional guide catheters 31. The System should have warranty of 05 years and after expiry of warranty, CAMC should be of 05 years. 32. The item should be BIS/ US FDA/ EU CE standard certified.
